become assumptions and internal results become subtasks.
(2) Proposer–reviewer pairs write the subtasks and harden the central question.
(3) An executed reference solution and a checker per subtask decide the answers; three quality checks
(cold solve, shortcut probe, consistency check) send the task back for revision or reject it.
(4) In Harbor, a solver is rewarded only if every checker passes.
